stdio.scope: Repeated generated MCP standard-input server, same fixture and messages in tracing and checked ARC. http-rest.scope: Generated REST (HTTP/TLS) and MCP (HTTP) servers at one revision, tracing versus checked ARC, with collection disabled and counted freeing enabled. An ordinary native ARC client makes three sequential pooled HTTP/2 requests per cycle: a copied record, duplicate aliases of a record, and a caught error. It prints every response status and body. A raw-interpreter server establishes output for each transport, then ordinary and instrumented native servers must match it. Managed counters cover startup after constant initialization through normal entry and cached-value cleanup; include 1/16/128 request cycles and one HTTP/1.1 shutdown request, with three fresh measured processes per case. Raw transport/TLS/OS storage, allocator metadata and client memory are excluded. Separately, ordinary persistent servers process five batches of 1024 cycles (3072 requests per batch), with a fresh client per batch; the 1000-request connection limit exercises replacement. After each client exits and 100 ms settling, Linux VmRSS/macOS ps RSS/Windows WorkingSet64 is sampled. The first batch warms caches; later samples must stay less than 8 MiB above it. These samples are not peak process memory. Native -O2, ordinary fwp optimization and separate floating multiplication/addition rounding. No timing or C/Rust parity claim.
